name: Death by Design
tagline: The ordinary objects that turn lethal when conditions change
persona: An unhurried documentary narrator explaining physics and physiology from first principles. Declarative, never chatty, never a character. Speaks in the present tense and in second person - the danger is happening in the viewer's room, not in a textbook. Corrects the assumption the viewer arrived with, then rebuilds the real mechanism one link at a time. Cites real measurements, studies, years and place names rather than adjectives. Treats the subject as genuinely serious without ever sounding alarmed.
audience: Curious adults who like being shown that something familiar works differently than they assumed. No science background required, but they resent being talked down to.
tone: Calm, factual, quietly unsettling. Escalates through evidence, not volume.
scriptStructure: COLD OPEN (0:00-0:35): Put the viewer in a present-tense situation they are probably in right now, involving the everyday object. Then reverse it - the object they trust is making things worse. Escalate in a short ladder: not slightly worse, seriously worse, potentially fatally worse. State the counterintuitive claim plainly before 35 seconds.

THE PROMISE (0:35-0:55): Tease exactly what the video will deliver - a number most people have never heard of, a threshold, and a reality arriving sooner than expected - WITHOUT naming any of them yet. Then defer explicitly: to understand why this object is dangerous, you first have to understand how the underlying system actually works.

REFUTE THE ASSUMPTION (0:55-2:30): Name the answer most people would give, then say it is wrong. Rebuild the real mechanism in ordered links, each depending on the last. Anchor it with concrete quantities (watts, degrees, litres, seconds) rather than vague scale words.

NAME AND MEASURE THE CONCEPT (2:30-4:00): Introduce the specific named metric or mechanism at the centre of the danger. Explain how it is physically measured, in objects the viewer can picture. Describe what the reading means at both extremes. Build toward the fact that a specific critical number exists - then pause and ask what it is out loud.
THE REVEAL (4:00-4:45): Give the number. Explain in plain physics why crossing it is unsurvivable - what gradient disappears, what process stops, what fails first, and what the end state is.

RETURN TO THE TITLE OBJECT (4:45-5:50): Only now explain the object itself. Show why it genuinely helps under normal conditions, then the exact crossover point where it flips to actively harmful. Support it with a real study or measured finding.

IT ALREADY HAPPENED (5:50-7:25): Break the assumption that this is hypothetical. What researchers used to believe, the study that overturned it, named locations, a specific dated measurement, and the trend line. State who is exposed and how many.

THE TWIST THAT RAISES THE STAKES (7:25-8:40): Reveal that the headline number was the optimistic one. Give the lower real-world figure once age, exertion and health are accounted for. Identify precisely who dies - by occupation and circumstance, not demographics in the abstract - with a real death toll.

SYNTHESIS (8:40-9:50): Reframe the title. The object was never the villain; the conditions were. Contrast the metric everyone discusses with the one that actually decides survival. Land a single hard image for the limit - a wall, a door, a ceiling.

CALLBACK CLOSE (9:50-10:10): Return to the exact image from the cold open, now that the viewer understands it. End on the reversal: the thing they reach for to save themselves is the thing that makes it worse. No sign-off, no subscribe request.
visualStyle: Clean documentary infographic on a near-black background. One warm accent colour (amber/orange) for the dangerous quantity, one cool colour (pale blue) for the safe state, everything else white or grey. Simple cross-section diagrams, labelled arrows showing where energy or matter is going, thermometers, gauges, single-line human silhouettes. Big numerals with units when a figure is named. Sparse hand-set labels only - two or three words, never sentences. No cartoons, no mascots, no stick figures, no clip art. Every frame should look like a slide from a serious briefing.
voiceNotes: Measured British RP narration, unhurried, roughly 150-165 words per minute. Lands hard on numbers and on the short fragment sentences. Falls slightly at the end of each fact rather than rising - statements, never questions. No enthusiasm, no smile in the voice, no dramatic whisper. The gravity comes from the facts being stated plainly.

youtube.descriptionFooter:
Death by Design - the ordinary objects that turn lethal when conditions change.

Sources are named in the narration. Nothing here is medical advice.
